text:
glasses_felix: I assumed a static location or a simple morning-to-night progression. Actually, it was at armchair_l1 late at night (22:59). Pattern: Felix leaves his glasses in the living room when relaxing, not just in the bedroom. Check armchair_l1 and coffee_table_l1 for evening queries.

glass_felix: I incorrectly assumed it moved to nightstand_b1 in the evening. Actually, it was at kitchen_table_k1 at 19:47 and 20:17, but at cupboard_k1 at 22:59. Pattern: The glass stays in the kitchen area but shifts between the table and cupboard. Do not check the bedroom nightstand. Check kitchen_table_k1 first, then cupboard_k1 for very late night.

mug_felix: I assumed it was in the kitchen cupboard. Actually, it was at kitchen_table_k1 in the morning. Pattern: Felix keeps his mug at the kitchen table, not in storage. Check kitchen_table_k1.

tablet_felix: I assumed it was at nightstand_b1. Actually, it was at kitchen_table_k1 in the morning. Pattern: Felix uses the kitchen table for his tablet in the morning, not the bedroom. Check kitchen_table_k1.

book_felix: I assumed it was at nightstand_b1. Actually, it was at armchair_l1 late at night. Pattern: Felix reads in the living room, leaving the book on the armchair. Check armchair_l1 for evening/night queries.

General Note: My default assumption that Felix’s items move to the bedroom (nightstand_b1) at night is incorrect. He frequently leaves items in the living room (armchair, coffee table) or kitchen (table, cupboard) depending on his activity. Do not default to nightstand_b1. Check living room and kitchen spots first for evening queries.
